THE DEFECT: section 10.2 explicitly frames itself as carrying T-347's "genuine detector-surface
gaps... found by this epic's own adversarial replay (T-347)" and does carry 3 of T-347's 5 named
cases (D: detector 2 blind on status=="superseded"; E: detector 4's case-sensitive scope match;
L: detector 4's subject-agnostic false-positive risk). It silently drops the other 2, both of
which I independently reproduced live against the real CLI just now, neither requiring any
tampering:

1) Case C (supersedes tier-bypass, needs zero tampering). PRECEDENT.md's section 1 headline
table and section 3 tie the whole tier ladder to "how much adversarial process a decision
survived" and state the risk neutralized by tier-symmetry as "a lower-authority record silently
outranking a higher one" -- but that protection, and the entire section-1 rule pairing it with a
named risk, is written only for overrules/voids. supersedes is never mentioned as an exception,
even though the shipped CLI's own module docstring says outright: "supersedes is deliberately
excluded: SDR-17.8 never applies a tier check to it." Reproduced in a fresh throwaway root:

  $ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py publish --root <tmp> --agent verifier-build-c --task T-345 \
      --title "tier1 anchor" --subject case-c-probe --tier 1 \
      --tier-evidence "event:2026-07-05T00:56:51Z" --ratio "tier1 baseline" --width narrow \
      --scope "role:worker" --revisit-trigger "never"
  published PR-001, exit=0

  $ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py publish --root <tmp> --agent verifier-build-c --task T-345 \
      --title "tier4 note superseding tier1" --subject case-c-probe --tier 4 \
      --tier-evidence "T-345" --width narrow --ratio "tier4 note overriding a tier1 record" \
      --supersedes PR-001
  published PR-002, exit=0

  $ python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('<tmp>/PR-001.json')); print(d['status'], d['superseded_by'])"
  superseded PR-002

  $ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py conflicts --root <tmp>
  conflicts: 0 findings across 2 record(s), exit=0

A tier-4, never-verdicted, single-agent note flipped a tier-1 "operator" record's status with a
plain publish call -- no refusal, no dangling-citation warning, no conflicts finding. This is a
STRICTLY STRONGER instance of the illegitimate-tier-inversion failure detector 3 exists to catch
(T-347's own framing), and it requires no hand-editing at all. Nowhere in PRECEDENT.md (section 1,
3, 7, 10.2, or 14) is supersedes named as exempt from tier-symmetry, and nowhere is this gap
recorded as a genuine gap the way D/E/L are.

2) Case G (dicta-embedded citation tokens invisible to both conflicts and cite --record).
Section 5.1/5.2 state the resolver walks a record's own cites/tier_evidence/relations[] fields;
what is never stated is that dicta (also a structural record field, section 4) is NOT among them,
so a PR-NNN/T-NNN-shaped string written only into dicta is invisible to every check. Reproduced:

  $ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py publish --root <tmp2> --agent verifier-build-c --task T-345 \
      --title "dicta dangling probe" --subject case-g-probe --tier 4 --tier-evidence "T-345" \
      --width narrow --ratio "structured ratio, no dangling tokens here" \
      --dicta "this cites PR-999 and T-999999 only in prose, never in cites[]"
  published PR-001, exit=0

  $ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite --root <tmp2> --record PR-001
  PR-001 cites T-345: OK          <- only the structured tier_evidence token is reported;
                                     nothing about the two prose-only dangling tokens in dicta
  exit=0

  $ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py conflicts --root <tmp2>
  conflicts: 0 findings across 1 record(s), exit=0

Both are real, live CLI behaviors (not simulated corruption), both were named by T-347 as genuine
gaps in the same note this revision explicitly cites and partially incorporates, and both are
squarely within this document's OWNS scope to name (section 10.2 already does exactly this for
sibling findings from the same source). This is a defect in T-345's execution of its own stated
method, not a request to touch precedent.py.
